source_lines.40: **Given:** Finite partial Boolean functions f and g with disjoint input blocks in the composition h=f∘g^N.
source_lines.58: 1.1 Let f:D_f→{0,1} be a nonconstant Boolean function on N bits and g:D_g→{0,1} a nonconstant Boolean function on m bits. The composed partial function h=f∘g^N has domain D_h={ (x_1,…,x_N)∈D_g^N : (g(x_1),…,g(x_N))∈D_f }. This domain is nonempty: choose one z∈D_f and fixed preimages in D_g of 0 and 1, which exist because g is nonconstant, then lift the coordinates of z blockwise. Choose optimal matrices Γ_f,Γ_g normalized so max_i||Γ_f∘Δ_i||=max_j||Γ_g∘Δ_j||=1; write a=||Γ_g||=Adv±(g). [given, F1, F2, F3, F6]
source_lines.60: 1.2 Decompose each adversary matrix by output classes, Γ_g=[[0,B_g],[B_g^T,0]]. For a,b∈{0,1}, let G^{ab} be the (a,b) block of Γ_g when a≠b and let G^{aa}=a I on D_g^a. For x,y∈D_h put \tilde x=(g(x_1),…,g(x_N)) and define (Γ_h)_{xy}=(Γ_f)_{\tilde x,\tilde y}\prod_{j=1}^N G^{\tilde x_j,\tilde y_j}_{x_j,y_j}. This matrix is real symmetric and vanishes whenever h(x)=h(y); if Γ_f,Γ_g are entrywise nonnegative, so is Γ_h. [given, F1, F2, F3, construct]
source_lines.62: 2.1 By [F4,F5], choose a singular-vector basis of the cross block B_g. Pair its positive singular vectors across the two output classes, and pair equal numbers of left and right null vectors with singular value zero. If the null-space dimensions differ, each leftover null vector is a one-dimensional component supported on just one output class; its equal-output patch is aI and its cross-output action is zero. For a paired singular value s≤a, the four restrictions G^{00},G^{01},G^{10},G^{11} act as a times C_s=[[1,s/a],[s/a,1]], which is positive semidefinite with unit diagonal. A leftover singleton is represented by C_0=diag(1,0) or diag(0,1), a positive semidefinite matrix with diagonal entries at most one. For each tuple of child components, the corresponding invariant subspace is indexed by the compatible outer output labels b∈D_f, and the restriction of Γ_h is a^N times the compression of Γ_f∘C, where C_{b,b′} is the product of the selected two-output factors. The tensor-product factor C is positive semidefinite with diagonal entries at most one. Write C_{b,b′}=⟨c_b|c_{b′}⟩ with ||c_b||≤1; then V|b⟩=|b⟩⊗|c_b⟩ is a contraction and V^*(Γ_f⊗I)V=Γ_f∘C, so ||Γ_f∘C||≤||Γ_f||. The SVD components span every child input space, proving ||Γ_h||≤||Γ_f||a^N. [given, F4, F5, step 1.2, algebra]
source_lines.64: 3.1 Choose top singular pairs (u_f,v_f) and (u_g,v_g) for the cross blocks of Γ_f and Γ_g. The bipartite block form makes α_f=(u_f,v_f)/√2 and α_g=(u_g,v_g)/√2 eigenvectors with eigenvalues ||Γ_f|| and a. For a fixed outer output tuple b, each child factor G^{b_j,b′_j} sends the restricted α_g component in class b′_j to a times the corresponding component in class b_j, whether b_j=b′_j (the patched aI block) or b_j≠b′_j (the singular-vector equation for B_g). Substitution in the definition of Γ_h therefore shows α_h(x)=α_f(tilde x)∏_jα_g(x_j) is an eigenvector with eigenvalue ||Γ_f||a^N. Together with step 2.1 this gives ||Γ_h||=||Γ_f||a^N. [given, F1, F4, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]
source_lines.66: 3.2 Fix an input bit q in block j and put d=||Γ_g∘Δ_q||. If d=0, then every entry of Γ_g∘Δ_q is zero, the equal-output patch dI is zero, and the masked composed block is zero. Suppose d>0. In Γ_h∘Δ_{j,q}, if the outer block outputs agree at j, its factor Γ_f∘Δ_j is zero; equivalently, the patched equal-output child block is diagonal in x_j and is killed by the inner mismatch Δ_q. If the outer outputs differ at j, the child cross block is exactly the corresponding block of Γ_g∘Δ_q. Thus the masked composite has the same entrywise construction as step 1.2 with outer matrix Γ_f∘Δ_j, child j cross block from Γ_g∘Δ_q patched by dI on equal-output blocks, and every other child patched by aI. Repeating the invariant-subspace and correlation-compression argument of step 2.1 bounds its norm by ||Γ_f∘Δ_j|| d a^{N−1}. The paired, zero-singular, and singleton components are handled as in step 2.1; the outer and inner filtered norms are at most one by normalization, so ||Γ_h∘Δ_{j,q}||≤a^{N−1}. [given, F3, F4, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1]
source_lines.68: 4.1 Therefore max_{j,q}||Γ_h∘Δ_{j,q}||≤a^{N-1}, while ||Γ_h||=Adv±(f)a^N by step 3.1. Its ratio is at least Adv±(f)a, proving Adv±(f∘g^N)≥Adv±(f)Adv±(g). If Γ_f and Γ_g are nonnegative, step 1.2 makes Γ_h nonnegative, so the identical argument proves Adv(f∘g^N)≥Adv(f)Adv(g). If either function is constant, the asserted lower bound is the trivial zero bound. [given, F1, F2, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

source_lines.61: 1.1 Let H=span{|start⟩}⊕(C^N⊗K⊗C²). The algorithm input requires |start⟩ to be unit and orthogonal to every query mode; hence |start⟩⟨start| is the orthogonal projection onto its span. It also labels the standard address basis by |i⟩=e_{i−1}, i∈[N]. Under the standard coordinate pairing in [F25], ⟨e_j,e_k⟩=Σ_rδ_{rj}δ_{rk}=δ_{jk}, so these address vectors and the response basis vectors are orthonormal. Therefore the query summands |i⟩⟨i|⊗I_K⊗|x_i⟩⟨x_i| are mutually orthogonal projections and are orthogonal to the start projection. Thus Π_x is an orthogonal projection. [given, F25, algebra]
source_lines.63: 2.1 Append a clean scratch bit u=0. In query mode, call O_x at address i to write u=x_i. In start mode route the oracle address to a fixed i_0∈[N] and apply H to u so the target is |+⟩; since X^{x_{i_0}}|+⟩=|+⟩, the unconditional oracle call leaves start unchanged. Apply a fixed phase −1 exactly when c=1, the mode is a query state, and z≠u; apply +1 on the start mode and when c=0. On query basis states this phase is +1 exactly when z=x_i, and −1 otherwise. [given, F21, F22, F23, step 1.1, algebra]
source_lines.65: 3.1 Call O_x again at the same address to reset u to 0 in query mode, using O_x²=I from [F22]. In start mode the second call again fixes |+⟩, and the final controlled H returns u to |0⟩. For c=1 the induced operator on H is 2Π_x-I; for c=0 it is I. Thus this fixed circuit realizes controlled R_{Π_x} with the plus-on-range sign specified in [F24], without a controlled unknown-oracle call. By linearity the same control/data action holds for arbitrary superpositions with the scratch returned clean. [given, F22, F23, F24, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

source_lines.34: In an SMP Equality protocol on n≥2 bits with worst-case error at most 1/3, no shared randomness or entanglement, and fixed q-qubit messages, each sender must transmit Ω(log n) qubits. For fixed Bob input y, the referee’s equality POVM separates ρ_y from each ρ_x, x≠y, by trace distance at least 1/3; packing d×d density matrices in trace distance yields 2ⁿ≤(26d^(3/2))^(d²), d=2^q, and hence q=Ω(log n).
